content_voiceover: Immune tolerance induction, or ITI, is the strategy for eradicating an inhibitor rather than just working around it. You give repeated, frequent doses of factor concentrate to retrain the immune system so it stops recognizing the factor as foreign. Regimens range from high dose, one hundred to two hundred international units per kilogram per day, down to low dose, fifty units per kilogram three times a week. Success rates differ sharply by disease: about seventy percent in hemophilia A but only around thirty percent in hemophilia B, which is part of why ITI is used more cautiously in B. For boards, know the good-risk predictors: a historical inhibitor peak under two hundred Bethesda units, a pre-ITI titer under ten BU, and an on-ITI peak that stays below two hundred fifty BU. Earlier initiation after inhibitor detection also improves the odds of success.
keypoints: ITI = repeated factor dosing to induce tolerance and eliminate inhibitor
Regimens: high dose 100-200 IU/kg/d vs low dose 50 IU/kg three times weekly
Success ~70% in hemophilia A, only ~30% in hemophilia B
Good-risk factors: pre-ITI titer <10 BU, historical peak <200 BU, on-ITI peak <250 BU, earlier start
keypoint_voiceover: Remember ITI as repeated factor dosing to retrain the immune system, with high or low dose options. Hemophilia A responds far better than B, about seventy versus thirty percent. Good prognosis comes from a low pre-ITI titer under ten Bethesda units, a historical peak under two hundred, an on-ITI peak under two hundred fifty, and starting early.
